problem: Existing human-aware VLN benchmarks (HA-VLN) use visually simplified gray SMPL humans and mix pedestrian priors into ordinary instructions, while social-navigation benchmarks are not language-conditioned. It is therefore hard to study goal-oriented VLN and dynamic-pedestrian safety jointly and in a controlled way.
motivation: Robots in human-populated spaces must ground language while reacting to moving pedestrians and keeping personal space. Success alone hides unsafe behaviour, so both navigation and social-safety metrics are needed. Separating ordinary route guidance from prior-augmented instructions allows controlled analysis of what pedestrian cues contribute.
key_idea: Build a Habitat 3.0 VLN benchmark with ORCA-controlled humanoid pedestrians, socially constrained expert paths, paired global and prior-augmented instructions, and joint success-safety metrics, plus a pedestrian-aware RL/IL baseline (DPet).
insight: Dynamic pedestrians mainly break reactive control, not language understanding. Zero-shot NaVILA's HCR rises from 2.11 (static) to 40.17 (dynamic) and StreamVLN's from 4.22 to 37.24. An RL policy trained only on static pedestrians drops from SR 34.53 to 27.69 when tested on dynamic ones, and adding prior instructions does not recover this, so social language needs embodied dynamic experience. The highest-SR method (DPet-RL) still has high HCR (42.45 under global instructions), and removing R_SCP lowers HCR (30.29) at the cost of SR (36.59), so success and safety trade off.
method: Benchmark/task: indoor Habitat 3.0 episodes with a Spot-like robot and humanoid pedestrians; the agent takes egocentric RGB-D plus an instruction and a start-relative pose, and stops within 3.0 m of the goal. 33,093 episodes (32,172 train, 921 val-unseen), each with two instructions.
Pedestrian simulation: humanoids move between assigned waypoints under an ORCA local policy, giving 1-6 agents per scene (3.21 per episode in episodes with pedestrians).

Expert trajectories: the A* shortest-path heading is blended with an ORCA-inspired avoidance heading, with a proximity-adaptive weight alpha of 0.5-0.95. A forward-suppression rule below 0.8 m clearance and deadlock recovery are added. Episodes are filtered by geodesic distance (at least 3.0 m) and final expert distance (within 1.0 m).

Hierarchical instructions: keyframes are chosen from action changes, pedestrian detections and the endpoints. A VLM produces static scene/object context and dynamic motion/risk/density context. Level-1 global instructions use static cues only; Level-2 prior-augmented instructions add concise dynamic-pedestrian cues.

DPet architecture: a CLIP RGB-D encoder and a language encoder are fused by cross-modal attention, then combined with a projection of the start-relative polar displacement and fed to an LSTM with policy and value heads.

DPet-RL: PPO with a task reward plus Social Cognition Penalties (collision and personal-space violation). Auxiliary heads, each weighted 0.1, predict visible pedestrian count, relative position and short-horizon motion; simulator pedestrian states serve only as training labels.
DPet-IL: behavior cloning on expert trajectories with cross-entropy weighted 3.0 at action-transition frames, sequences capped at 400 steps.
VLM baselines: NaVILA and StreamVLN are LoRA fine-tuned on 3,000 sampled examples from all 561 training scenes for 5 epochs.

setting.backbone: DPet (CLIP visual encoder + language encoder + cross-modal attention + LSTM, trained from scratch for the policy); baselines NaVILA and StreamVLN (VLM-based, zero-shot and LoRA fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: DPed-VLN train split (32,172 episodes); DPet-IL uses all of it and DPet-RL trains online with PPO. VLM baselines are LoRA-tuned on 3,000 sampled examples.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + instruction + start-relative polar displacement
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: STOP / FORWARD / TURN-LEFT / TURN-RIGHT
setting.privileged: none at test time (pedestrian states used only as auxiliary training labels)

results: On DPed-VLN val-unseen, DPet-RL reaches SR/SPL/STL of 37.13/33.36/36.83 with global instructions and 38.55/36.35/37.97 with prior-augmented ones, well above NaVILA-FT (22.37 SR under global instructions) and StreamVLN-FT. Its HCR stays high (36.70-42.45), while fine-tuned StreamVLN and DPet-IL have the lowest collision rates (about 26-28%) at much lower SR. LoRA fine-tuning gives modest gains, e.g. StreamVLN HCR 37.24→27.14 under global instructions.
limitations: The benchmark has only train and val-unseen splits, with a single 921-episode evaluation set. VLM baselines are fine-tuned on only 3,000 examples, so the VLM comparison is not at full scale.
The best-SR policy still collides in 37-42% of episodes, and there are no real-robot experiments. Instructions are VLM-generated, and the Level-2 gains are small (about 1-2 SR points).
The DPet architecture is simple (an LSTM policy), and the ablations show only modest, metric-dependent gains from the auxiliary losses and SCP reward.
